90 /*
91 * Persistent configurations - start
92 * Client persistent configuration aging is refreshed on persistent configurations set
93 * persistent configuration of aged clients removed from the persistent-db and cleared in the runtime-db
94 */
95
96 // Indicates when client parameters were last updated (even if not updated yet to persistent-db)
97 // minimal value is used as invalid value.
98 std::chrono::system_clock::time_point parameters_last_edit =
99 std::chrono::system_clock::time_point::min();
100
101 // Optional - if configured the client has its own configured timelife delay.
102 std::chrono::minutes time_life_delay_minutes =
103 std::chrono::minutes(beerocks::PARAMETER_NOT_CONFIGURED);
104
105 sMacAddr initial_radio = beerocks::net::network_utils::ZERO_MAC;
106
107 // If enabled, the client will be steered to the initial radio it connected to - save at initial_radio.
108 son::eTriStateBool stay_on_initial_radio = son::eTriStateBool::NOT_CONFIGURED;
109
110 // The selected bands that the client should be steered to.
111 // Default value is PARAMETER_NOT_CONFIGURED - which means no limitation on bands.
112 // Possible values are bitwise options of eClientSelectedBands.
113 uint8_t selected_bands = beerocks::eFreqType::FREQ_UNKNOWN;
114
115 // The unfriendly status indicates how we interact with the client.
116 // If the unfriendly status is not configured, the client is assumed friendly unless proven otherwise.
117 // The friendliness status affects how we handle the aging mechanism.
118 son::eTriStateBool is_unfriendly = son::eTriStateBool::NOT_CONFIGURED;
119
120 /*
121 * Persistent configurations - end
122 */
